ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Dark Star & Good Lovin' with tight rhythm and soaring leads
ai_show_review.blurb: The second set erupts with a smoking Dark Star that segues into Saint Stephen and a double Not Fade Away. China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider shines in the first set, while the encore Good Lovin' delivers an electrifying climax. Overall the show is a high‑octane snapshot of the spring‑71 Dead.
ai_show_review.review: April 8, 1971 at Boston Music Hall finds the Dead locked in on a fiery groove that barely lets up. The first set opens with Truckin' and Bertha before moving into a standout China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider where Pigpen’s electric piano adds a bright texture to Bob’s searing solo. A solid run of Sugar Magnolia, Casey Jones and the rest of the set leads into an explosive second half: Dark Star bursts open the set with Jerry’s crystal‑clear lead work, flowing seamlessly into Saint Stephen and a double Not Fade Away that drives the band into a tight, propulsive jam. The highlight reel continues with Sing Me Back Home, a rousing Good Lovin' that showcases Phil’s “magnificent” bass foundation, and an encore where the rhythm section locks in on another powerful Good Lovin' finish. Across all six soundboard sources the performance remains consistently high‑energy, with the Deibert recording offering the cleanest mix and most balanced instrument placement.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crisp mix, balanced instrument placement and minimal noise, making the intricate jams most audible.

key_highlights: Smoking Dark Star that launches into Saint Stephen and a double Not Fade Away
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider shines with bright electric piano texture
Powerful Good Lovin' encore driven by Phil’s spectacular bass work
Crystal‑clear Bertha and Truckin' showcase Bob’s forward rhythm guitar

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers an incredible tone and soaring leads on Dark Star, Good Lovin' and throughout the set, with crisp placement in the mix.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a spectacular, often described as ‘magnificent’ bass foundation that drives the extended jams, especially during Dark Star and the Second That Emotion debut.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar is forward and vivid on Bertha, Truckin' and the China > Rider segue; his vocal contributions add weight to the ballads.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann lays down a solid, steady pulse that underpins the high‑energy second set, keeping the jams tight.
